sections.label: Wakaf management and disbursement
sections.summary: Wakaf assets are managed by Warees Investments, MUIS and approved mutawallis, with a MUIS committee reviewing annual disbursements.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The wakaf assets are managed by Warees Investments, a subsidiary of MUIS, and the appointed mutawallis, in accordance with the intentions of the wakif or donor.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: First, all mutawallis must be approved by the MUIS Council and have the competencies to maintain good governance and long-term sustainability of the wakaf they oversee.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Third, the MUIS Wakaf Disbursement Committee, which comprises members from the MUIS Council, monitors and reviews annual wakaf disbursements, and makes recommendations on the allocation of wakaf funds, in accordance with the wakif’s intention.

sections.label: Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme
sections.summary: MUIS and Warees have undertaken asset enhancement and redevelopment under the Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme to optimise returns while sustaining heritage value.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For some wakaf properties, MUIS and Warees have also undertaken asset enhancement and redevelopment initiatives under the Wakaf Revitalisation Scheme to optimise financial returns while sustaining their heritage value.

sections.label: 2024 wakaf disbursements
sections.summary: In 2024, $11.3 million was disbursed to wakaf beneficiaries, including family members, mosques, madrasah, community organisations and charities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2024, a total of $11.3 million was disbursed to the wakaf beneficiaries, which include the family members of the benefactors, as well as mosques, madrasah, community organisations and charities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Depending on the intention of the wakif, these returns may be used to build and maintain mosques and madrasahs, support the poor and needy, and also, fund the development and welfare of the community.

sections.label: Jamae Chulia restoration assurance
sections.summary: The Jamae Chulia Mosque restoration is completed and the Jamae Chulia Heritage will be completed soon, with assurance that wakif intentions are held in trust.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As the Member can see, the Jamae Chulia Mosque restoration has been completed and the Jamae Chulia Heritage is going to be completed soon.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And not only do we want to develop for today, I think the key, what I got from my engagement, is that the community leaders want to do this for the future generation as well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, I assure the Member that we will do our best to ensure that what the wakif would like to leave behind is not only acceded to, but we hold it with trust.
